new.analysis:
## What happened

You were set up for three walk-run sessions and ran none; Tuesday, Thursday, Friday and Sunday were planned rest and stayed rest. You wrote that you felt great going into the week, so I am reading this as life getting in the way rather than a body problem. If something else was going on, tell me in the next check-in and I will adjust.

## Why this plan

I am not trying to make up the missed week, and I am not pushing harder than where you left off. Monday and Wednesday repeat the eight by two-minute run with one-minute walk that you handled well two weeks ago. That rebuilds the rhythm without asking anything new of the legs.

Saturday is the one small step forward: six by three minutes running with one-minute walks. The longest continuous run so far was two minutes, so three minutes is the next honest stretch. Keep the run bouts at the same easy effort you have been using; heart rate under about 145 is the right zone.

## Looking ahead

With six weeks to the Corrowmore Harvest 5K, we need the long run to grow from under three kilometres toward five by early November. That is very doable if we get three sessions in each week from now. The main thing this week is simply to get out the door on Monday, Wednesday and Saturday.
